title: After ban of one stun grenade, French police continue to use a different model
subhead: France's Interior Ministry suspended the use of the EF-SON stun grenade after a 15-year-old high school student lost his hand on October 5. Another stun grenade, the GL-304, was used on October 6 at Place de la Bastille, lightly injuring two people.

A disastrous day for French supermarkets after massive cyberattack targets refrigeration systems
subhead: Freezers and cold-storage rooms at several hundred stores overheated overnight from October 11 to 12, causing tons of merchandise losses. The vulnerability, linked to software made by the Danish company Danfoss, has been identified. France's cybercrime office has opened an investigation.

title: Oxfam sues French state over tax inequality: 'Wealthiest buy privilege of not following same rules'
subhead: Oxfam France has filed a lawsuit against the French state over its tax system, accusing it of 'no longer adequately guaranteeing' equality before taxation.

title: Local authorities authorize killing of aggressive chamois who attacked joggers in eastern France
subhead: Two runners were charged by the wild animal just days apart. Faced with this unusually aggressive behavior, the prefect has ordered that the chamois be identified and killed.

title: Why Ceuta and Melilla remain a point of contention between Spain and Morocco
subhead: The arrival of more than 72,000 migrants in Ceuta from Morocco this summer reignited the debate over Spain's sovereignty on the two autonomous cities on the North African coast. Morocco has claimed this sovereignty since the 1960s, and King Felipe VI's planned visit on October 13 is intended as yet another symbolic rejection of those claims.

From farms to high schools, France is a nation on edge
subhead: The country is wavering between revolt and despair as it faces a whirlwind of crises: devastating heatwaves, spiralling debt, spiking interest rates, rising cost of living, housing shortages, increasing unemployment and protests over conditions in high schools.

title: Glucksmann won the center-left primary. He must now unite his camp
subhead: Raphaël Glucksmann won the center-left primary in the first round on Sunday, with 66% of the vote. He called for a 'break with Macronism' and an end to 'Jean-Luc Mélenchon's dominance over the left,' while insisting the main opponent remained 'the far right.'

title: How the French left wants to reclaim the idea of the nation
subhead: Although the concept of the nation was born during the French Revolution, the far right has claimed it since the end of the 20th century. Nevertheless, the left has never completely abandoned patriotism. The current presidential campaign proves as much.
